How to use this calculator

  1. Enter annual income / taxable estate, deduction or exemption, assumed effective tax rate.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How estate tax is calculated

The entered rate is applied as one effective rate to the amount remaining after the deduction or exemption. Many tax systems use brackets, credits and special rules, so this is a scenario estimate. Formula: Estimated estate tax = max(0, estate value − assumed exemption) × entered rate. Use the displayed details to inspect the intermediate amounts and replace example assumptions with terms from your own quote or records.

Estimated estate tax = max(0, estate value − assumed exemption) × entered rate.
A worked example

A $2 million estate, $1 million assumed exemption and 20% rate produce a $200,000 estimate.

Assumptions & useful context

Rate and deduction are user assumptions. Tax is progressive in many jurisdictions; this flat-rate estimate is not a tax return.

Financial projections use your assumptions. Actual returns, lender terms, fees and tax rules can differ; these results do not guarantee a future outcome.

Frequently asked questions

Estate Tax Calculator: what does the result include?

No. It applies the one effective rate you enter after the deduction or exemption. Set that rate to your own planning assumption.

Estate Tax Calculator: which assumptions matter most?

Only if you reflect their effect in the effective rate. The estimate does not look up current tax rules or determine filing eligibility.
